intro.title: :has()
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive webpage that uses the CSS `:has()` pseudo-class to style elements based on their contents. You will learn how `:has()` allows you to select and style a parent element when it contains specific child elements, enabling more dynamic and conditional styling without JavaScript. The main technologies involved are pure CSS, focusing on selectors and pseudo-classes. By the end, you will understand the syntax and practical applications of `:has()` to create responsive and context-aware designs.
intro.usecase: The :has() selector is commonly used in modern web applications to create dynamic, context-aware interfaces. For instance, in a dashboard with collapsible panels, you can use :has() to style a panel's header differently when its content section is expanded. In complex forms, you can highlight a fieldset when any of its required inputs are invalid. E-commerce sites often use :has() to apply special styling to product cards that contain a 'sale' badge or out-of-stock label. This allows developers to write cleaner CSS that responds to the actual state of the DOM without adding extra JavaScript classes.
